title: delta-driven-sustained-throughput-calibrator-and-util-sampler
author: Priya Natarajan
description: Motivation: customers running long-lived Dedicated workloads see transient spikes that trigger aggressive autoscaling and then rapid decommits which increase cost and instability. This PR introduces a delta-driven calibrator that smooths sustained throughput signals, plus a sampled utilization inspector that provides lower-cost telemetry for warm-pool fidelity decisions. Goals: reduce oscillatory scale-ups from short bursts, provide a conservative reservation throttle when sustained demand drifts above commitment, and surface sampled util metrics for fleet-level dashboards. Design summary: 1) Delta-driven Sustained Throughput Calibrator: computes a smoothed delta of per-tenant throughput over multiple time windows (1m, 5m, 30m) and converts positive sustained deltas into a bounded 'credit request' instead of immediate node allocation. The calibrator exposes a configurable hysteresis and backoff curve to avoid repeated churn. 2) Sampled Utilization Inspector: lightweight agent that samples core utilization (GPU cycles, queue depth, tail latency) at sub-second cadence but reports aggregated sketches (Hdr hist + p50/p90/p99) at a lower telemetry rate. Sampling reduces telemetry cost while preserving signals for warm-pool fidelity heuristics. 3) Reservation Throttle Adapter: when calibrator detects sustained upward drift beyond tenant's committed throughput fraction, the adapter applies a soft throttle that reduces new burst-grant window sizes and nudges requests to a fallback model variant when available. Implementation notes: - New controller implemented in controllers/delta_calibrator.go with 3 window decayers and an adjustable sigmoid backoff; core compute path is ~120 LOC. Key snippet (simplified): if util_delta > surge_threshold { credit = min(max_credit, base_credit * sigmoid(util_delta)); requestCredit(tenant, credit) } - Sampled inspector implemented as a worker in telemetry/inspector_worker.go; reports sketches to telemetry/v2/sampled; uses reservoir sampling and HDR sketches. - Reservation throttle hooks into allocation/orchestrator.go as a low-cost gating filter applied after normal admission checks. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind EXP_DELTA_CALIBRATOR; staged rollout to 10% of Dedicated capacity, monitor rollout_linear ENG-1298. Backwards compatibility: controller is additive and off by default. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for calibrator windows and backoff - [x] Integration test that simulates sustained 5m ramp - [x] Telemetry tags and dashboards (WIP) - [x] Docs changes in ./docs/dedicated/autoscale.md (brief guide) Related: builds on telemetry-sampling proposal in ENG-1442 and addresses customer complain SUP-4012.

review_comments: Jonah Blake: Can you clarify how the calibrator interacts with existing warm-pool prewarming? We should not starve warmlets during long ramps.

Author (Priya): The calibrator issues credit requests instead of immediate node creation; warm-pool prewarm still runs but is deprioritized for credits under the soft throttle. Added comment in allocation_orchestrator.go to make ordering explicit.
María González: The sigmoid parameters are sensitive — add conservative defaults and an escape hatch flag for hotfixing. Also add more unit tests around near-threshold behavior.
Author: Added serde for sigmoid params and unit tests covering edge cases. Also added an override env var DELTA_CALIBRATOR_HARD_DISABLE for emergency kill.
Aisha Khan: CI failed on lint on first run because of protobuf formatting; please run protoc formatter in the CI step to avoid flakes.
Author: Fixed formatting and re-ran CI, green now.
release_notes: Introduce Delta-driven Sustained Throughput Calibrator (feature-flagged) and Sampled Utilization Inspector. Reduces oscillatory scale-ups for Dedicated tenants and provides sampled telemetry to inform warm-pool fidelity. Disabled by default; enable via EXP_DELTA_CALIBRATOR. See docs/dedicated/autoscale.md for usage and tuning guidance.
